lines.text: Meet Sam. About five hours a day, Sam's world fits in a glowing rectangle.
Every swipe is a tiny gamble. Will the next one be good?
That not knowing releases dopamine, the brain's want more signal. It fires for the chase, not the prize.
The part that says enough, the prefrontal cortex, keeps wiring until around age twenty five.
At night, screen light tells the body it's still day. Melatonin, the sleep signal, waits. And kids' eyes are extra sensitive.
The good news? Young brains are built to change. Sleep, play, and real faces rebuild them.
Screens aren't poison. They're powerful. Balance is the skill.
